item.title: Contratto di ricerca: Characterization of the transmission dynamics of Xylella fastidiosa by insect vectors in vineyards and semi-natural environments (Univ. BARI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-20 23:55
Institution: Univ. BARI, Lussemburgo
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-05 Patologia vegetale ed entomologia

*Xylella fastidiosa* subsp. *fastidiosa* Sequence Type 1 (Xff-ST1) represents a new threat to European viticulture, particularly in light of its detection in table grape vineyards in Apulia. The project aims to understand the epidemiology of *Xylella fastidiosa* in table grape vineyards and to investigate the role of spontaneous vegetation and non-cultivated environments in supporting insect vector populations and acting as sources or recipients of the bacterium. The results will improve the understanding of vector-pathogen-host interactions, identify key epidemiological risk factors, and provide data useful for risk assessment and the development of effective disease management strategies.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: IpD52/2026:"Study of the Influence of Soil, Climatic, and Technological Factors on the Variability and Characterization of the Sensory Space of Lugana Wine " (Univ. VERONA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-23 13:00
Institution: Univ. VERONA, Verona
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-07 Scienze e tecnologie alimentari

The research program aims to characterize the sensory space of Lugana wines through two complementary approaches: Quantitative Descriptive Analysis (QDA) and fast profiling (FP) techniques. QDA, conducted by a trained panel, will enable the identification and quantification of the wines’ olfactory, gustatory, and visual attributes. FP methods will be used to explore sensory similarities and differences among samples, identifying groups of wines and their characteristic descriptors. Integrating these two approaches will make it possible to define and compare the sensory spaces of wines from different areas, highlighting their distinctive characteristics and variability. item.title: Incarico post-doc: IpD51/2026:"Physiological and agronomic characterization of TEA grapevine prototypes genetically improved for tolerance to biotic and abiotic stresses." (Univ. VERONA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-23 13:00
Institution: Univ. VERONA, Verona
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-03 Scienze e tecnologie dei sistemi arborei e forestali

The research program focuses on the phenotyping of gene-edited grapevine plants during the field-testing phase. The vines to be characterized are TEA plants edited for genes associated with susceptibility to downy and powdery mildew, as well as for metabolic pathways involved in grape quality. Activities will entail agronomic characterization and the monitoring of physiological parameters to evaluate plant performance in the cultivation environment, in relation to genotype and in response to potential abiotic stresses (e.g., water deficit).

item.description:

Institution: Univ. VERONA, Verona
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-06 Genetica, chimica e pedologia agraria e forestale

Research activity supports the continuation of breeding programs aimed at developing new disease-resistant and high quality grapevine varieties for more sustainable viticulture, reducing the impact of polluting substances and working in close collaboration with the industrial partner. At the same time, the project aims to explore the feasibility of implementing a genomic selection approach, already widely applied in animal breeding, with the objective of optimizing and accelerating the identification and selection of the most promising grapevine genotypes. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Development of oilseed crops for the bio-based industry (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-20 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-02 Agronomia e sistemi colturali erbacei e ortofloricoli

The researcher will conduct agronomic field trials at the University Experimental Farm and/or other experimental sites. The researcher will be directly involved in experimental design, establishment and management of field trials, collection of agronomic and physiological measurements, data management and statistical analysis, and reporting and dissemination of results through workshops, scientific conferences, and project meetings.The researcher will also supervise PhD students and other staff involved in research activities at the same experimental sites. Basic knowledge of statistical methods and a good command of English are required.
